_doc: The edit decision list for film/build/edit.py. Captions are templates filled from facts.json ({key}); a caption
with a figure that isn't a fact fails the build. Times are seconds of film time. A time may name a mark in the
beat's events.json instead: 'name', 'name=value' (any data field), '#n' for the nth match (1-based), then an
optional offset ('scrub-start+0.4', 'end'). Caption times are relative to the beat's output; segment in/out
are capture times. A value given as {"16x9": …, "9x16": …} differs by aspect. Speed ≠ 1 shows a ×N badge.
'band': 'top-right' moves a beat's caption box off the UI it would cover (16:9 only; 9:16 captions sit below the app).
Credit chips come from the capture's 'clip' marks (the engines whose clips are in view). The loop has no
overlays, so it must come from a stretch with no clip playing (P01: the Tax drag; P10: the results, which name the models).

captions.text: Same panel, same camera push. Line drift from frame 0: Wan 2.2 {hook_wan_line} px, Gen-4.5 {hook_g45_line} px.
Wan 2.2 wins on stability. It also barely moved: {hook_wan_flow} px of median optical flow, against {hook_g45_flow}.

card.title: Is the stability score measuring stability, or stillness?
card.sub: {n_clips_total} generated clips, each beside the hand-drawn still it was made from.

captions.text: Pick a panel and an engine on the contact sheet.

text.16x9: est-line-1, asked to stay idle. Line drift: Gen-4.5 {pick_line} px, Wan 2.2 {pick_wan_line} px.
text.9x16: est-line-1, asked to stay idle. Gen-4.5's line drift: {pick_line} px.

captions.text: Scrub the curve and the clips follow, frame by frame. The curve is the line art's chamfer distance to frame 0.
The difference view: each clip minus its own first frame. Black means unchanged.
Across the {n_engines} engines, the ones that move more drift more: ρ {rho}, exact p {p_exact}.

text.16x9: In gold: Gen-4.5, which moves most, then Wan 2.2, which moves least.
text.9x16: Gen-4.5 moves most and Wan 2.2 least.

captions.text: The Stillness Tax, an exploratory lens: charge each engine for its motion.
At price 0 it is the paper's ranking, and Wan 2.2 leads. Raise the price per doubling of motion…
LTX-2.3 leads only from {x_ltx} to {x_g45} px. From {x_g45} px per doubling of motion, Gen-4.5 leads.
Gen-4.5's rank changes because it moves more, not because it looks better.

card.title: Price the motion in, and the ranking becomes a choice you can see.
card.sub: A case for evaluating world models with motion priced in, not on stability alone.

p10.title: blindpanel
p10.chip_note: hidden from raters on the page

captions.text: {n_raters} raters scored {n_study_clips} generated clips, blind to the model. Your turn.
First the source stills on their own, then each clip beside its still.
Two questions per clip: does it still look hand-drawn, and is it still the same picture?
A scripted run for the film: each answer is the panel's rounded mean, nudged by a fixed seed.
Where you land: your agreement with the panel's average, beside each rater's.
The panel itself agrees only modestly: α {alpha_register} on register, {alpha_sameness} on sameness.
It is all computed in your browser. Nothing is sent unless you opt in.
The kit behind it: one study file, one command. A fresh clone installs, builds, checks both example studies and serves one.
